data.function: P2 report: watchdog reset pad state
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim says no source shows that a watchdog reset returns the coprocessor's outputs to their reset state. That is too broad. The datasheet does show it for a watchdog configured the way pico-sdk 2.3.0 configures it, and for Bank 0 pins that are in use. The claim reads the 9.3 sentence ("If a pad's isolation latches are in the latched state ... does not physically return the pad to its reset state") as if it covered every pad. It only covers latched pads. A pin in use is not latched, because gpio_set_function() clears ISO (9.3 IMPORTANT box, 9.7 NOTE). The claim also treats "ISO resets to 1" as general. Section 9.7 ties that to the switched core domain isolation signal, which POWMAN asserts around a power-down of the switched core domain. It also says the PADS register block reset does not reset the ISO bits, and that "resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state". The chain that shows the return is as follows. First, watchdog_enable() sets every PSM_WDSEL bit except ROSC and XOSC (watchdog.c line 53, hw_set_bits, so RESETS, bit 4 of Table 532, is set). Second, a watchdog timeout makes the PSM restart from the point WDSEL selects (7.4, 7.4.3). The RESETS stage is the master subsystem reset (7.4.1 step 5: "does not remove individual subsystem resets"). Third, the RESET register resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) at 0x1, so both are held in reset (Table 535). Fourth, a non-isolated pad therefore returns to its reset state (9.7). The 9.3 reset state is output buffer high-impedance, input disabled, pulled low, IO muxing at the null function. Table 528 lists WATCHDOG RESET PSM with no power-state change, so the switched core does not power down and ISO is not set again. What stays not shown is narrower. The first case is a watchdog set to a switched-core or POWMAN-level reset through POWMAN_WATCHDOG (Table 528: SWCORE, POWMAN, POWMAN ASYNC → P0.0). There the domain powers down, pads keep their last output state, and ISO resets to 1 until software clears it (9.7). The second case is a watchdog set up without PSM_WDSEL.RESETS, or with firmware other than pico-sdk's watchdog_enable(). The image enables no watchdog yet (IOBoard.md:221), so which setup it uses is not stated. None of this is measured. The ruling is about this figure, not about the part's identity or lifecycle.
data.evidence: RP2350 datasheet build-date 2025-07-29, SHA-256 2877d0f270fb6d6a57943bee58aaad536aa027bea1e5b1c4ce2541a3230d4be8, the same file the claim cites. 9.3: the pads return to reset state on brownout, RUN low, CDBGRSTREQ and rescue reset. "If a pad's isolation latches are in the latched state (Section 9.7) then resetting the PADS and IO registers does not physically return the pad to its reset state." IMPORTANT box: "The gpio_set_function() SDK function performs these tasks automatically" (IE=1, ISO=0). 9.7: "The ISO control bits (e.g. GPIO0.ISO) are reset by the top-level switched core domain isolation signal, which is asserted by POWMAN before powering down the switched core domain ... The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads." Table 528: WATCHDOG RESET PSM row is all dashes, including Power State; WATCHDOG SWCORE, POWMAN and POWMAN ASYNC RESET go to P0.0. 7.4: "A partial sequence runs after a write to the FRCE_OFF register or a watchdog timeout"; 7.4.1 step 5: "Deasserts the master subsystem reset, but does not remove individual subsystem resets"; 7.4.3: "The watchdog can trigger a full or partial sequence by writing to the WDSEL register". Table 532 (PSM WDSEL): bit 4 RESETS, reset value 0x0. Table 535 (RESETS RESET): bit 9 PADS_BANK0 and bit 6 IO_BANK0, both RW, reset value 0x1. 12.9.4: PSM_WDSEL triggers system resets through a full or partial PSM sequence; RESETS_WDSEL triggers subsystem resets; POWMAN_WATCHDOG triggers chip-level resets. pico-sdk 2.3.0 watchdog.c line 53: hw_set_bits(&psm_hw->wdsel, PSM_WDSEL_BITS & ~(PSM_WDSEL_ROSC_BITS | PSM_WDSEL_XOSC_BITS)). The verifier quoted this line as an assignment; it is a bit-set, which has the same effect here. IOBoard.md:221 (the coprocessor enables the RP2350 watchdog, the image enables none yet) and :340 (load gates at reset) in checkout e13f5f60d2e5.
